patient.title: Alectinib monotherapy
patient.context_label: ALK-positive NSCLC · adjuvant or advanced disease
patient.scope_note: This guide covers alectinib alone for ALK-positive lung cancer. Confirm whether it is adjuvant treatment after complete surgery, first treatment for advanced cancer, or treatment after crizotinib. These settings have different evidence and treatment lengths.
patient.indication_text: Alectinib targets an abnormal ALK growth signal. After complete surgery the aim is to reduce the chance of cancer returning; in advanced cancer the aim is to control the cancer. Your team explains the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty.
patient.purpose: Alectinib targets an abnormal ALK growth signal. After complete surgery the aim is to reduce the chance of cancer returning; in advanced cancer the aim is to control the cancer. Your team explains the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty.
patient.schedule_summary: Take alectinib twice daily with food, every day, with no planned rest week. After surgery, treatment lasts up to 24 months, stopping sooner for recurrence or unacceptable side effects. For advanced cancer, treatment continues until progression or unacceptable side effects under the oncology plan.
patient.administration_text: The usual starting dose is 600 mg twice daily: four 150 mg capsules each time, taken with food. Use your own prescription, which may specify a lower dose. Swallow capsules whole; do not open or dissolve them. If a dose is missed, take it only if the next dose is more than 6 hours away. If the next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose at its usual time; do not take an extra dose.
patient.monitoring_summary: Liver profile every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then every 4 weeks or as clinically indicated. FBC and renal profile every 4 weeks. CPK every 2 weeks for the first month, then as clinically indicated, including muscle symptoms. Blood pressure and pulse as clinically indicated. NCCP says ECG prior to cycle 2, then as indicated; a continuous oral regimen has no defined cycle length, so agree the first repeat ECG appointment locally. Assess symptoms, interactions, adherence, current dose and treatment benefit; scans and disease monitoring follow the Consultant plan.

agents.name: Alectinib
agents.mechanism: Blocks an abnormal ALK growth signal
agents.explanation: Alectinib blocks the abnormal ALK protein that drives growth in ALK-positive cancer cells. It can act against cancer in the body and brain. It can also affect healthy tissues, so blood tests and symptom checks remain important.
agents.watch: Take with food. Keep blood tests and report muscle weakness, breathing changes, jaundice or dizziness promptly.
risks: Muscle pain or weakness and raised CPK
Liver injury and raised liver tests or bilirubin
Anaemia, including destruction of red blood cells (haemolysis)
Slow heart rate, dizziness or fainting
Lung inflammation (ILD/pneumonitis), which can be serious
Skin rash and sensitivity to sunlight
Gastrointestinal perforation; urgent severe abdominal pain
Potential harm to a developing baby

support.text: Alectinib is minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Treat nausea with prescribed as-required medicine if needed. Routine preventive anti-sickness treatment and infusion premedication are not required; your team selects a suitable rescue medicine.

support.text: The usual starting dose is 600 mg twice daily: four 150 mg capsules each time, taken with food. Use your own prescription, which may specify a lower dose. support.title: Muscles, liver, blood and breathing
support.text: Keep liver, CPK and blood-count appointments. Muscle symptoms, jaundice, dark urine, unusual fatigue, cough or breathlessness need prompt review even between appointments.

support.title: Heart rate and other medicines
support.text: Tell the team about dizziness, fainting and medicines that slow the pulse. Check new prescriptions, supplements, grapefruit and Seville oranges with pharmacy; interactions may require closer monitoring rather than an automatic dose change.

support.title: Sun protection
support.text: Avoid prolonged sunlight during treatment and for at least 7 days after stopping. Use broad-spectrum UVA/UVB sunscreen and lip balm SPF 50 or higher.

support.title: Pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding
support.text: Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 weeks afterwards. Men with female partners who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months afterwards. Oral contraceptive effectiveness may be reduced: ask for a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility before treatment and contact the team promptly if pregnancy occurs.

anatomy: Report promptly because lung inflammation can occur.
A slow pulse can be symptomatic and needs medicine review.
Liver injury may start silently; keep tests and report yellow skin or dark urine.
Anaemia can include red-cell breakdown; report marked changes.

evidence.title: Evidence differs after surgery and in advanced cancer
evidence.intro: Studies describe groups in a particular setting. Ask which comparison applies to you.
evidence.population: Completely resected ALK-positive NSCLC; untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC; or advanced cancer after crizotinib, studied separately.
evidence.interpretation: After complete surgery, ALINA found that alectinib delayed cancer recurrence compared with platinum chemotherapy; whether it improves overall survival remains uncertain. In untreated advanced cancer, ALEX showed better cancer control than crizotinib, but its final survival comparison did not establish a clear overall-survival difference. Separate studies showed tumour responses after crizotinib. These groups cannot predict your personal outcome or rank all current treatment choices.
evidence.limitations: The after-surgery study does not yet establish a survival benefit. Advanced-disease trials do not compare every modern ALK medicine. Group averages do not predict an individual result.

questions.q: Does taking capsules mean fewer important risks?
questions.a: Capsules are cancer treatment and can cause serious side effects. Keep the planned tests and use the oncology contact plan for new symptoms.

questions.q: Does having side effects show it is working?
questions.a: No. Side effects do not reliably indicate cancer response; your team assesses benefit using the relevant follow-up plan.

questions.q: How long will I take alectinib?
questions.a: Take alectinib twice daily with food, every day, with no planned rest week. After surgery, treatment lasts up to 24 months, stopping sooner for recurrence or unacceptable side effects. For advanced cancer, treatment continues until progression or unacceptable side effects under the oncology plan.

questions.q: What if I miss a dose or vomit?
questions.a: If a dose is missed, take it only if the next dose is more than 6 hours away. If the next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose at its usual time; do not take an extra dose.
Liver tests are planned every 2 weeks for 3 months. CPK is checked every 2 weeks for the first month. Blood count and kidney tests are checked every 4 weeks; symptoms may prompt extra tests.
NCCP asks for an ECG before its second treatment cycle, but this medicine is taken continuously. Ask the team to confirm the first repeat ECG appointment and later checks.

questions.q: Can I change or restart my dose myself?
questions.a: No. If alectinib is held or reduced, ask what needs to recover, when review happens and who will authorise restarting.

questions.q: What should I say when calling?
questions.a: Give the medicine name, current dose, last dose, symptoms and when they began. Explain whether you can drink, pass urine and manage usual activities. Do not delay calling to collect details.

questions.q: Can I use this page to decide whether tests are safe?
questions.a: No. Blood results, symptoms, current dose and treatment history need the prescriber’s assessment. This guide does not authorise treatment.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. This map shows general timing. Your hospital arranges actual appointments.

clinical.component_rationale: Alectinib blocks the abnormal ALK protein that drives growth in ALK-positive cancer cells. It can act against cancer in the body and brain. It can also affect healthy tissues, so blood tests and symptom checks remain important.
key_points: Separate 00401a post-crizotinib, 00401b first-line advanced and 00401c adjuvant after complete resection.
600 mg twice daily with food continuously; reduction levels 450 then 300 mg twice daily; discontinue if 300 mg twice daily cannot be tolerated.
Adjuvant maximum 24 months; advanced until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Minimum 7-day crizotinib washout for 00401a.
ILD at any grade needs interruption; permanent discontinuation requires no other potential cause.
CPK >5 versus >10 ×ULN and recurrence have different restart pathways. Haemolysis needs haemoglobin and diagnostic context.
Combined liver-test permanent-stop rule requires exclusion of cholestasis/haemolysis.
Bradycardia grade, contributing medicine adjustment and recurrence determine restart/stop advice; no imported QTcF cutoff.
NCCP and current SmPC support Child-Pugh C starting dose 450 mg twice daily; severe renal impairment/dialysis does not automatically require a reduction.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Alectinib targets an abnormal ALK growth signal. After complete surgery the aim is to reduce the chance of cancer returning; in advanced cancer the aim is to control the cancer. Your team explains the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Adult ALK-positive advanced NSCLC previously treated with crizotinib.
Adjuvant after complete resection in adult ALK-positive NSCLC at high risk of recurrence. NCCP: stage IB (tumour ≥4 cm) to IIIA, ECOG 0–1.
eligibility_orientation: Confirm ALK-positive NSCLC by a validated test; establish indication, staging/resection and prior-treatment history.
FBC, renal and liver profile, CPK, blood pressure and ECG before treatment.

For treatment after crizotinib allow a minimum 7-day washout. For adjuvant treatment confirm complete resection, high-risk criteria and ECOG 0–1.
important_cautions: ALINA studied completely resected stage IB (tumour ≥4 cm)–IIIA disease using AJCC/UICC 7th edition. Modern stage labels require mapping, not automatic substitution.
ALINA compared 24 months of alectinib with four cycles of platinum chemotherapy; it did not test routinely adding alectinib after adjuvant chemotherapy.

ALINA 2025 updated disease-free results are a conference analysis with 8 December 2024 efficacy cutoff; overall survival remained immature. Do not translate DFS into proven survival or individual cure estimates.
ALEX studied untreated advanced disease against crizotinib, not other modern ALK inhibitors. Final OS HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.56–1.08) did not establish a statistically significant OS difference.
Ou phase II was a single-arm post-crizotinib study, mostly previously chemotherapy-treated; response rates do not establish comparative survival benefit.
NCCP 00401c lists reimbursement N/A. NCCP indication, EMA licence, trial population and current access/reimbursement are separate facts.

This guide covers alectinib alone for ALK-positive lung cancer. Confirm whether it is adjuvant treatment after complete surgery, first treatment for advanced cancer, or treatment after crizotinib. These settings have different evidence and treatment lengths.

Take alectinib twice daily with food, every day, with no planned rest week. After surgery, treatment lasts up to 24 months, stopping sooner for recurrence or unacceptable side effects. For advanced cancer, treatment continues until progression or unacceptable side effects under the oncology plan.

support_plans.label: Alectinib daily oral treatment
additional_support: Alectinib is minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Treat nausea with prescribed as-required medicine if needed. Routine preventive anti-sickness treatment and infusion premedication are not required; your team selects a suitable rescue medicine.

The usual starting dose is 600 mg twice daily: four 150 mg capsules each time, taken with food. Use your own prescription, which may specify a lower dose. Swallow capsules whole; do not open or dissolve them. If a dose is missed, take it only if the next dose is more than 6 hours away. If the next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, take the next dose at its usual time; do not take an extra dose.
Keep liver, CPK and blood-count appointments. Muscle symptoms, jaundice, dark urine, unusual fatigue, cough or breathlessness need prompt review even between appointments.

Tell the team about dizziness, fainting and medicines that slow the pulse. Check new prescriptions, supplements, grapefruit and Seville oranges with pharmacy; interactions may require closer monitoring rather than an automatic dose change.
Avoid prolonged sunlight during treatment and for at least 7 days after stopping. Use broad-spectrum UVA/UVB sunscreen and lip balm SPF 50 or higher.

Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 weeks afterwards. Men with female partners who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months afterwards. Oral contraceptive effectiveness may be reduced: ask for a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility before treatment and contact the team promptly if pregnancy occurs.

guidance.label: NCCP oral minimal–low risk: as-required antiemetics only; NCIS V8 checked separately
